build.note: the switches a .jsc producer must share with this profile. A cache produced by a build that differs in `sandbox` or `pointerCompression` cannot be read with this profile: the trusted-pointer slot widths differ, so every object after the first trusted field is misread rather than refused. The header carries no field that states them, so a reader can only check them against what it knows about the producer.

unresolvedGlobalConstants.note: globals.h constexprs whose right-hand side we do not evaluate (sizeof/offsetof of C++ types, or arch reservation sizes). None of them feeds an emitted table; they are listed so the gap is visible.

unknownConditionIdentifiers.note: identifiers that appeared in a #if while expanding the root headers and are not in the defines map, so they evaluated to 0 (the C rule). All of these guard compiler-attribute macros in src/base/macros.h, not list content; the root-order acceptance check confirms the lists are unaffected.

enumValueDisagreements.note: members whose Torque declaration position is not their C++ value. The C++ value is authoritative and is what layouts.json -> enums.<X>.members carries; the Torque order is kept as enums.<X>.torqueDeclarationOrder. These are not errors: for an `extern enum` Torque declares names only. They are listed because reading one of them as a value is a wrong-but-plausible answer.

functionKindPredicates.note: predicates in src/objects/function-kind.h whose body is not a disjunction of base::IsInRange / equality tests, so no ordinal range is emitted for them. They are left out rather than approximated.
